purpose: Apply user-confirmed closures, speed reductions or travel-time increases and compare the same uploaded transport system before and after the change.

execution_tiers.name: Grounded location change
execution_tiers.claim: Where the confirmed direct changes occur. No network propagation is inferred.

execution_tiers.name: Deterministic network test
execution_tiers.claim: Reachability, harmonic-efficiency and reproducible proxy-route response under a fixed disclosed demand design

execution_tiers.name: MATSim exploratory probe
required_data: positive free-flow travel time or derivable impedance
execution_tiers.claim: Agent-event, queue and rerouting sensitivity for a deterministic probe population. It is not observed demand or calibrated congestion.

execution_tiers.name: MATSim uploaded-demand experiment
required_data: at least two routable directed links
positive road length and speed, travel time or free-flow time on every routable link
positive uploaded capacity on every routable link
execution_tiers.claim: Paired baseline-versus-disruption agent simulation using the uploaded demand and supply assumptions

operators.closure: Remove the selected directed link from the deterministic network test. The MATSim scenario retains it with near-zero capacity and very low speed so affected agents can be recorded as queued or stuck.
operators.speed_reduction: Multiply free-flow impedance by 1/(1-r), with 0 < r <= 0.95.
operators.travel_time_increase: Multiply free-flow impedance by 1+m, with m > 0.

impedance_precedence: observed travel time at the chosen timestamp
time derived from observed speed and uploaded length
uniform hop count for the topology-only network test

matsim_contract.interoperability: The Python adapter writes standard MATSim network and population inputs, then launches a process-isolated Java worker.
matsim_contract.paired_design: Baseline and disrupted runs use the same population, random seed, sample factor and iteration count.
matsim_contract.replanning: The worker uses ReRoute with weight 0.2 and ChangeExpBeta with weight 0.8.
matsim_contract.queue_supply: The uploaded-demand tier uses positive uploaded hourly capacity on every routable link. The probe tier labels the 900 vehicles/hour numerical default. Every exported link currently uses one lane, and QSim flow and storage capacity factors use the disclosed population sample factor.
matsim_contract.calibration_boundary: Uploaded-demand means the uploaded demand and supply were used. Field calibration is claimed only when an independent calibration record accompanies those inputs.

primary_sources.citation: Horni, A., Nagel, K. and Axhausen, K.W. (eds.) (2016). The Multi-Agent Transport Simulation MATSim. London: Ubiquity Press.
primary_sources.relationship: Authoritative MATSim reference for agent plans, QSim network loading, scoring and iterative replanning.

primary_sources.citation: Jenelius, Petersen and Mattsson (2006), Importance and exposure in road network vulnerability analysis
Jenelius and Mattsson (2012), Road network vulnerability analysis of area-covering disruptions
Nagurney and Qiang (2008), A network efficiency measure with application to critical infrastructure networks. Journal of Global Optimization, 40, 261-275.
Faturechi and Miller-Hooks (2014), Travel time resilience of roadway networks under disaster

randomness: The deterministic network test has no random component. MATSim uses a recorded fixed seed. Exact repeatability also requires the same Java, MATSim build, thread configuration and job inputs.
verification: one final operator per uploaded link
all selected keys belong to the current uploaded project
baseline and scenario use the same node and link identity contract
paired MATSim jobs use identical demand and seed
event totals reconcile with returned completed and stuck trips
sample factor and capacity factors are recorded
probe and uploaded-demand claims remain separate
known_limitations: A topology-only or probe run cannot estimate observed traffic demand, congestion, population impact or evacuation clearance.
A few or zero indirectly loaded roads can be a valid result when the tested relations become disconnected. The run must report completed, rerouted and disconnected relations separately.
The worker does not include reference-project calibration targets or location-specific assumptions.
No casualty estimate, emergency dispatch order or live traffic-control instruction is inferred.
